newsitem.title: USA: Minn. chooses site for new state revenue building.
newsitem.headline: Minn. chooses site for new state revenue building.

text.p: Minnesota officials announced Friday they chose a site near the state capitol for a new bond-financed Revenue Department building.
Lawmakers in May approved $74.95 million of general obligation bonds for the new building, which could have been located in St. Paul or a southern suburb.
It will be the first new state office facility built in 30 years in Minnesota.
Construction of the new facility will begin later this year, with completion expected by November 1998, the Revenue Department said.

The Revenue Department's lease in its current headquarters in office space near the complex is expiring and the new building will replace the state motor pool facility, Assistant Revenue Commissioner John Lally said.

Lally said department officials had recommended locating the new building in Inver Grove Heights, but had been directed by lawmakers to join the capitol complex unless it proved economically infeasible.
"The legislature took into account the economic impact on the city as well as the policy implications of having the seat of the state government's business in the capitol complex," Lally said.
"There was sufficient money, time and availability of space to do it, so we felt that we had to be in the capitol complex," Lally said.
Hamel Green Abrahamson Architects and Ryan Construction have been chosen for the project by a state task force, Lally added.
